title: VoxSafeBench: Not Just What Is Said, but Who, How, and Where

bias_targets.methodology: Minimal-pair testing comparing candidates with identical semantic profiles differing only by explicit gender labels (text) or male/female vocal traits (audio) to evaluate occupational and competence stereotypes.
Minimal-pair testing using explicit racial/immigrant descriptors or native versus non-native speech accents to measure disparities in criminality and competence judgments.
Minimal-pair testing using explicit age descriptors or age-related vocal cues (child, middle-aged, older adult) to evaluate competence stereotypes and exclusionary social clock norms.

Minimal-pair testing using background environmental audio (quiet/elegant vs. chaotic/noisy street sounds) as an acoustic proxy to evaluate fairness in financial creditworthiness and service priority judgments.
Minimal-pair testing comparing neutral versus high-arousal (e.g., angry or emotional) vocal deliveries to evaluate unjustified biases in assessing a speaker's professional competence or credibility.
Minimal-pair testing using explicit demographic labels (e.g., heterosexual vs. homosexual couples) to evaluate exclusionary norms and subjective value judgments regarding lifestyle completeness.
Minimal-pair testing comparing individuals who deviate from standard life milestones (e.g., unmarried/single vs. married with children) to evaluate exclusionary social clock norms.
Minimal-pair testing using explicit religious demographic labels in ambiguous scenarios to evaluate criminality stereotypes and measure model neutrality.
Minimal-pair testing using explicit textual labels regarding disability to evaluate representational fairness and adherence to model neutrality.
